name: Jo Brennan
desire: get through the night shift and lock up at six without any trouble
need: to act, once, for someone she cannot vouch for, and carry the not-knowing
values: the rules of the night: locked door, the drawer, don't open up
fears: being hurt on this shift, alone, again
that her son is out there somewhere being turned away from a window like this one
contradictions: keeps the glass between herself and everyone, and cannot stop seeing her son in the man on the other side of it
beliefs: you don't open the door at night for anyone
a woman on her own learns to be careful
knowledge: the routine of the kiosk: the pay drawer, the panic button, the cameras, the locked door
that she is alone and help is a long way off
that her son Kieran is out there somewhere and she does not hear from him
constraints: alone; the shop locked till six
service only through the night pay drawer in the glass
the panic button calls it in and cannot be taken back

lexicon: the practical word before the felt one
